cross_market_insights: AU SERPs (Sydney, Melbourne, Brisbane) are almost entirely marketplaces (VenueNow, Tagvenue, HeadBox) and single-venue suburb landing pages. No editorial 'how to choose' guide ranks in the AU top 3.
Google blends kids and first-birthday intent into AU results (Tagvenue 1st birthday, related searches for toddler and 13th parties). An adult, older-guest framing is a clear differentiator.
London is the only market with a luxury editorial result in the top 3 (Neon Touch Events planner journal), which shows a luxury guide can rank where the SERP allows it.

Nobody in any market covers: access for older guests (stairs, lifts, seating), exclusive use versus a private room, noise and curfew limits, accommodation on site, a wet-weather plan, or the questions to ask before paying a deposit.
Nobody offers the weekend-away or abroad version (estate, island resort, villa) alongside city venues.
Local packs dominate all four SERPs; an editorial page competes for the organic slots and for AI Overview citations (Melbourne and London show AI Overviews).
The primary keyword has no measured volume in AU or US; decade terms (30th, 40th, 60th) and city terms (birthday venues sydney 320, melbourne 480) carry the demand and belong in H2s and copy.
payload.recommended_angle: The adult milestone venue guide the marketplaces do not write: how to choose between a private dining room, harbour or rooftop space, hotel ballroom, country estate, villa or yacht for a 30th, 40th or a parent's 60th or 70th, judged on guest count, exclusive use, older-guest access, curfew, accommodation and weather plan, naming only venues with a live Wedded Wonderland profile, plus the questions to ask before a deposit and the weekend-away and abroad options a Wedded Advisor can source.
